verses.text: Quid ergo dicémus? permanébimus in peccáto ut grátia abúndet?
Absit. Qui enim mórtui sumus peccáto, quómodo adhuc vivémus in illo?
An ignorátis quia quicúmque baptizáti sumus in Christo Jesu, in morte ipsíus baptizáti sumus?
Consepúlti enim sumus cum illo per baptísmum in mortem: ut quómodo Christus surréxit a mórtuis per glóriam Patris, ita et nos in novitáte vitæ ambulémus.
Si enim complantáti facti sumus similitúdini mortis ejus: simul et resurrectiónis érimus.

responsory.text: Ecce Agnus Dei, ecce qui tollit peccáta mundi: ecce de quo dicébam vobis: Qui post me venit, ante me factus est:
responsory.repeat: Cujus non sum dignus corrígiam calceaménti sólvere.

responsory.text: Qui de terra est, de terra lóquitur: qui de cælo venit, super omnes est.
Cujus non sum dignus corrígiam calceaménti sólvere.

parts.title: Lesson from the letter of St. Paul the Apostle to the Romans

verses.text: What shall we say, then? shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?
God forbid. For we that are dead to sin, how shall we live any longer therein?
Know you not that all we, who are baptized in Christ Jesus, are baptized in his death?
For we are buried together with him by baptism into death; that as Christ is risen from the dead by the glory of the Father, so we also may walk in newness of life.
For if we have been planted together in the likeness of his death, we shall be also in the likeness of his resurrection.

responsory.text: Behold the Lamb of God, behold Him Which taketh away the sins of the world; behold Him of Whom I said unto you: He That cometh after me is preferred before me
responsory.repeat: Whose shoe's latchet I am not worthy to unloose.

responsory.text: He that is of the earth speaketh of the earth; He That cometh from heaven is above all.
Whose shoe's latchet I am not worthy to unloose.

verses.text: Hoc sciéntes, quia vetus homo noster simul crucifíxus est, ut destruátur corpus peccáti, et ultra non serviámus peccáto.
Qui enim mórtuus est, justificátus est a peccáto.
Si autem mórtui sumus cum Christo, crédimus quia simul étiam vivémus cum Christo,
Sciéntes quod Christus resúrgens ex mórtuis jam non móritur: mors illi ultra non dominábitur.
Quod enim mórtuus est peccáto, mórtuus est semel: quod autem vivit, vivit Deo.
Ita et vos existimáte vos mórtuos quidem esse peccáto, vivéntes autem Deo, in Christo Jesu Dómino nostro.

responsory.text: Dies sanctificátus illúxit nobis: veníte, gentes, et adoráte Dóminum:
responsory.repeat: Quia hódie descéndit lux magna in terris.

responsory.text: Hæc dies quam fecit Dóminus, exsultémus et lætémur in ea.
Quia hódie descéndit lux magna in terris.

verses.text: Knowing this, that our old man is crucified with him, that the body of sin may be destroyed, to the end that we may serve sin no longer.
For he that is dead is justified from sin.
Now if we be dead with Christ, we believe that we shall live also together with Christ:
Knowing that Christ rising again from the dead, dieth now no more, death shall no more have dominion over him.
For in that he died to sin, he died once; but in that he liveth, he liveth unto God:
So do you also reckon, that you are dead to sin, but alive unto God, in Christ Jesus our Lord.

responsory.text: This day which is breaking is holy; O come, ye Gentiles, and worship the Lord.
responsory.repeat: For this day is much light come down unto us from heaven.

responsory.text: This is the day which the Lord hath made, let us rejoice and be glad in it.
For this day is much light come down unto us from heaven.

verses.text: Non ergo regnet peccátum in vestro mortáli córpore ut obediátis concupiscéntiis ejus.
Sed neque exhibeátis membra vestra arma iniquitátis peccáto: sed exhibéte vos Deo, tamquam ex mórtuis vivéntes: et membra vestra arma justítiæ Deo.

responsory.text: Benedíctus qui venit in nómine Dómini, Deus Dóminus, et illúxit nobis:
responsory.repeat: Allelúja, allelúja.

responsory.text: Hæc dies quam fecit Dóminus, exsultémus et lætémur in ea.
Allelúja, allelúja.

verses.text: Let no sin therefore reign in your mortal body, so as to obey the lusts thereof.
Neither yield ye your members as instruments of iniquity unto sin; but present yourselves to God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of justice unto God.

responsory.text: Blessed be He That cometh in the name of the Lord! God is the Lord Who hath showed us light.
responsory.repeat: Alleluia, Alleluia.

responsory.text: This is the day which the Lord hath made, let us rejoice and be glad in it.
Alleluia, Alleluia.

verses.text: Peccátum enim vobis non dominábitur: non enim sub lege estis, sed sub grátia.
Quid ergo? peccábimus, quóniam non sumus sub lege, sed sub grátia? Absit.
Nescítis quóniam cui exhibétis vos servos ad obediéndum, servi estis ejus, cui obedítis, sive peccáti ad mortem, sive obeditiónis ad justítiam?
Grátias autem Deo quod fuístis servi peccáti, obedístis autem ex corde in eam formam doctrínæ, in quam tráditi estis.
Liberáti autem a peccáto, servi facti estis justítiæ.

responsory.text: Hic qui advénit, nemo scit nomen ejus nisi ipse solus: † vocátur verbum Dómini habens vestem præcláram:
responsory.repeat: Et omnis chorus Angelórum in albis sequúntur eum.

responsory.text: Oculi ejus velut flamma ignis: † et in cápite ejus diadémata multa.
Et omnis chorus Angelórum in albis sequúntur eum.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
Et omnis chorus Angelórum in albis sequúntur eum.

verses.text: For sin shall not have dominion over you; for you are not under the law, but under grace.
What then? Shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace? God forbid.
Know you not, that to whom you yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants you are whom you obey, whether it be of sin unto death, or of obedience unto justice.
But thanks be to God, that you were the servants of sin, but have obeyed from the heart, unto that form of doctrine, into which you have been delivered.
Being then freed from sin, we have been made servants of justice.

responsory.text: This is he who comes, whose name no man knows but he himself; he is called the word of the Lord, dressed in shining clothes
responsory.repeat: And all the choirs of angels followed him, dressed in white.

responsory.text: His eyes were as a flame of fire, and on his head were many diadems.
And all the choirs of angels followed him, dressed in white.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
And all the choirs of angels followed him, dressed in white.

parts.title: Sermo sancti Augustíni Epíscopi
paragraphs: Dóminus noster Jesus Christus, fratres caríssimi, qui in ætérnum est cunctórum Creátor, hódie de matre nascéndo factus est nobis Salvátor. Natus est nobis hódie in témpore per voluntátem, ut nos perdúcat ad Patris æternitátem.

responsory.text: Congratulámini mihi, omnes qui dilígitis Dóminum:
responsory.repeat: Quia, cum essem párvula, plácui Altíssimo, et de meis viscéribus génui Deum et hóminem.

responsory.text: Beátam me dicent omnes generatiónes, quia ancíllam húmilem respéxit Deus.
Quia, cum essem párvula, plácui Altíssimo, et de meis viscéribus génui Deum et hóminem.

parts.title: A sermon of St. Augustine, Bishop.
paragraphs: Our Lord Jesus Christ, dearest brethren, who in eternity is the Creator of all things, was as at this time born of a mother and became our Saviour. It was as at this time that he willed to be born for us in earthly time, so as to lead us to the Father's eternity.

responsory.text: Rejoice with me, all ye that love the Lord.
responsory.repeat: For while I was yet little I pleased the Most High, and from my womb have I brought forth God and man.

responsory.text: All generations shall call me blessed, for God hath regarded the lowliness of His hand-maiden.
For while I was yet little I pleased the Most High, and from my womb have I brought forth God and man.

paragraphs: Factus est Deus homo, ut homo fíeret Deus: ut panem Angelórum manducáret homo, Dóminus Angelórum hódie factus est homo. Hódie impléta est prophetía illa, quæ dicit: Roráte, cæli, désuper, et nubes pluant justum: aperiátur terra, et gérminet Salvatórem.

responsory.text: Confirmátum est cor Vírginis, in quo divína mystéria, Angelo nuntiánte, concépit: tunc speciósum forma præ fíliis hóminum castis suscépit viscéribus:
responsory.repeat: Et benedícta in ætérnum, Deum nobis prótulit et hóminem.

responsory.text: Domus pudíci péctoris templum repénte fit Dei: intácta nésciens virum, verbo concépit Fílium.
Et benedícta in ætérnum, Deum nobis prótulit et hóminem.

paragraphs: God is made man, that man may be made as God. That man may eat Angels' food, the Lord of Angels was as on this day made man. Now is fulfilled that prophecy: Drop down, ye heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down righteousness: let the earth open, and bring forth a Saviour.

responsory.text: The heart of the Virgin was fixed, when the Angel declared unto her the mystery of God, and she conceived, then did she receive in her pure womb Him That is fairer than the children of men.
responsory.repeat: And, she that is blessed for ever, brought forth for us God and man.

responsory.text: Soon rises, in that modest shrine, The Temple of the Lord Divine The stainless and unwedded one, Within her womb conceived the Son.
And, she that is blessed for ever, brought forth for us God and man.

paragraphs: Factus est ígitur qui fécerat, ut invenirétur qui períerat. Sic enim in Psalmis homo confitétur: Priúsquam humiliárer, ego peccávi. Peccávit homo, et factus est reus: natus est homo Deus, ut liberarétur reus. Homo ígitur cécidit, sed Deus descéndit. Cécidit homo miserabíliter, descéndit Deus misericórditer; cécidit homo per supérbiam, descéndit Deus cum grátia.

responsory.text: Benedícta et venerábilis es, Virgo María, quæ sine tactu pudóris invénta es mater Salvatóris:
responsory.repeat: Jacébat in præsépio, et fulgébat in cælo.

responsory.text: Dómine, audívi audítum tuum, et tímui: considerávi ópera tua, et expávi: in médio duórum animálium.
Jacébat in præsépio, et fulgébat in cælo.

paragraphs: He who made all things is therefore himself made, that those who are lost may be found. It is even as man is made to testify of himself in the Psalms: Before I was humbled, I went wrong. Man sinned and became guilty. God is born man, that the guilty may be delivered. Man fell, but God descended. Man fell miserably, God descended mercifully. Man fell by pride, God descended with grace.

responsory.text: Blessed and worshipful art thou, O Virgin Mary; from thee, still maiden undefiled, the Saviour came a little Child.
responsory.repeat: He Whose glory filled the heavens lay in a manger.

responsory.text: O Lord, I have heard thy speech and was afraid; I considered thy works and trembled. O Thou That dwellest between the two living creatures!
He Whose glory filled the heavens lay in a manger.

paragraphs: O mirácula, o prodígia, fratres mei! Natúræ jura mutántur in hómine; Deus náscitur, virgo sine viro gravidátur, viri nésciam sermo Dei marítat: simul facta est mater et virgo; mater facta, sed incorrúpta; virgo habens fílium, nésciens virum; semper clausa, sed non infœcúnda. Solus enim sine peccáto est natus, quem sine viríli compléxu non concupiscéntia carnis, sed obediéntia génuit mentis.

responsory.text: In própria venit, et sui eum non recepérunt: † quotquot autem recepérunt eum, dedit eis potestátem fílios Dei fíeri:
responsory.repeat: Qui non ex sanguínibus, neque ex voluntáte carnis, neque ex voluntáte viri, sed ex Deo nati sunt.

responsory.text: Si autem filii, et herédes: † herédes, quidem Dei, coherédes autem Christi.
Qui non ex sanguínibus, neque ex voluntáte carnis, neque ex voluntáte viri, sed ex Deo nati sunt.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
Qui non ex sanguínibus, neque ex voluntáte carnis, neque ex voluntáte viri, sed ex Deo nati sunt.

paragraphs: O my brethren, what a miracle! what a wonder! The laws of nature are changed concerning man: God is born, a Virgin conceiveth without an husband; the Word of God is wedded to one who knoweth no man; she is at once Mother and Virgin. A Mother, yet inviolate: a Virgin having a Son; knowing no man, ever sealed, yet not unfruitful. For he alone was born without sin. He alone was born without human embrace, begotten not of the will of the flesh, but of the obedience of the mind.

responsory.text: He came unto his own, and his own received him not. But as many as received him, he gave them power to be made the sons of God:
responsory.repeat: Who are born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.

responsory.text: And if sons, heirs also; heirs indeed of God, and joint heirs with Christ.
Who are born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
Who are born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.

parts.title: Léctio sancti Evangélii secúndum Matthǽum
paragraphs: In illo témpore: Defúncto Heróde, ecce, Angelus Dómini appáruit in somnis Joseph in Ægýpto, dicens: Surge, et áccipe Púerum et Matrem ejus, et vade in terram Israël: defúncti sunt enim, qui quærébant ánimam Pueri. Qui consúrgens, accépit Púerum et Matrem ejus, et venit in terram Israël. Audiens autem, quod Archeláus regnáret in Judæa pro Heróde patre suo, tímuit illo ire: et, admonítus in somnis, secéssit in partes Galilææ. Et véniens habitávit in civitáte, quæ vocátur Názareth: ut adimplére tur quod dictum est per Prophétas: Quóniam Nazaræus vocábitur.

parts.title: Homilía sancti Hierónymi Presbýteri
parts.source: Liber 1 in Comment. in cap. 2 Matthæi
paragraphs: Ex hoc loco intellígimus non solum Heródem, sed et sacerdótes et scribas eódem témpore necem Dómini fuísse meditátos. Qui surgens accépit púerum, et matrem ejus. Non dixit: Accépit fílium suum et uxórem suam, sed Púerum et matrem ejus; quasi nutrítius, non marítus.

responsory.text: Sancta et immaculáta virgínitas, quibus te láudibus éfferam, néscio:
responsory.repeat: Quia quem cæli cápere non póterant, tuo grémio contulísti.

responsory.text: Benedícta tu in muliéribus, et benedíctus fructus ventris tui.
Quia quem cæli cápere non póterant, tuo grémio contulisti.

parts.title: From the Holy Gospel according to Matthew
paragraphs: In that time: When Herod was dead, behold an angel of the Lord appeared in sleep to Joseph in Egypt, Saying: Arise, and take the child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel. For they are dead that sought the life of the child. Who arose, and took the child and his mother, and came into the land of Israel. But hearing that Archclaus reigned in Judea in the room of Herod his father, he was afraid to go thither: and being warned in sleep retired into the quarters of Galilee. And coming he dwelt in a city called Nazareth: that it might be fulfilled which was said by the prophets: That he shall be called a Nazarene.

parts.title: Homily by St. Jerome, Priest (at Bethlehem.)
parts.source: Bk. i., Comm. on Matth. ii.
paragraphs: From the words, they are dead, (in the Plural), which are used in this passage of the Gospel, we may understand that there were others beside Herod which sought the young Child's life probably the Priests and Scribes. And he Joseph arose, and took the young Child and His Mother. It is not written, He took his wife and child, but he took the young Child and His Mother; whence it is clear that the holy Evangelist willeth to imply that Joseph was not the father, but the Guardian of Jesus, not the husband, but the Betrothed of Mary.

responsory.text: O how holy and how spotless is thy virginity; I am too dull to praise thee:
responsory.repeat: For thou hast borne in thy breast Him Whom the heavens cannot contain.

responsory.text: Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb.
For thou hast borne in thy breast Him Whom the heavens cannot contain.

paragraphs: Audiens autem quod Archeláus regnáret in Judǽa pro Heróde patre suo, tímuit illo ire. Multi labúntur erróre propter ignorántiam históriæ, putántes eumdem esse Heródem, a quo in passióne sua Dóminus irridétur, et qui nunc mórtuus esse referátur. Ergo Heródes ille qui cum Piláto póstea amicítias fecit, hujus Heródis fílius est, frater Archelái.

responsory.text: Nésciens Mater Virgo virum, péperit sine dolóre:
responsory.repeat: Salvatórem sæculórum, ipsum Regem Angelórum, sola Virgo lactábat úbere de cælo pleno.

responsory.text: Domus pudíci péctoris templum repénte fit Dei: intácta nésciens virum, verbo concépit Fílium.
Salvatórem sæculórum, ipsum Regem Angelórum, sola Virgo lactábat úbere de cælo pleno.

paragraphs: But when he heard that Archelaus did reign in Judea, in the room of his father Herod, he was afraid to go thither. There are some persons so grossly ignorant of history that they confuse themselves over the two Herods, as if the one mentioned here were the same who afterwards set our Lord at nought during His Passion, and they cannot understand how he should now be said to be dead. The Herod who was made friends with Pilate over Christ's death, was the son of the Herod who massacred the infants of Bethlehem, and the brother of Archelaus.

responsory.text: The Virgin-Mother that knew not a man, bore, but travailed not.
responsory.repeat: She fed the Saviour of the world, The King of Angel hosts above, Jesus, our Redeemer blest, From the fountain of her breast.

responsory.text: Soon rises in that modest shrine, The Temple of the Lord Divine; The stainless and unwedded one, Within her womb conceived the Son.
She fed the Saviour of the world, The King of Angel hosts above, Jesus, our Redeemer blest, From the fountain of her breast.

paragraphs: Quóniam Nazarǽus vocábitur. Si fixum de Scriptúris posuísset exémplum, numquam díceret: Quod dictum est per prophétas: sed simplíciter: Quod dictum est per prophétam. Nunc autem pluráliter prophétas vocans, osténdit se non verba de Scriptúris sumpsísse, sed sensum.

responsory.text: Párvulus natus est nobis, et fílius datus est nobis, † et factus est principátus super húmerum ejus:
responsory.repeat: Et vocábitur Admirábilis, Deus Fortis.

responsory.text: Multiplicabitur ejus imperium, † et pacis non erit finis.
Et vocábitur Admirábilis, Deus Fortis.

paragraphs: He shall be called a Nazarene. The Evangelist, in quoting these words, saith that they were spoken by the Prophets, (Plural). If he had been citing any one precise passage he would have said by the Prophet, in the Singular. But he is citing the sense of the Prophets, and not any individual passage in any of their writings. He seemeth to refer to the fact that in Hebrew the word Nazarene signifieth holy, and that Christ is the Holy One of God is the common declaration of all the Scriptures.

responsory.text: A child is born to us, and a son is given to us, and the government is upon his shoulder:
responsory.repeat: And his name shall be called, Wonderful, God the Mighty.

responsory.text: His empire shall be multiplied, and there shall be no end of peace.
And his name shall be called, Wonderful, God the Mighty.

paragraphs: Nazarǽus sanctus interpretátur; sanctum autem Dóminum futúrum omnis Scriptúra commémorat. Póssumus et áliter dícere; quod étiam eísdem verbis, juxta hebráicam veritátem, in Isaía scriptum sit: Exiet virga de radíce Jesse, et Nazarǽus de radíce ejus conscéndet.

responsory.text: O Regem cæli, cui talia famulántur obsequia: stábulo pónitur, qui cóntinet mundum:
responsory.repeat: Jacet in præsépio, et in cælis regnat.

responsory.text: Natus est nobis hódie Salvator, qui est Christus Dóminus, in civitáte David.
Jacet in præsépio, et in cælis regnat.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
Jacet in præsépio, et in cælis regnat.

paragraphs: He seemeth to refer to the fact that in Hebrew the word Nazarene signifieth holy, and that Christ is the Holy One of God is the common declaration of all the Scriptures.

We can even state in a different way that which is written in the same words, according to the Hebrew text, in Iasiah: “There shall come forth a rod out of the root of Jesse, and the Nazarene shall rise up out of his root.”

responsory.text: How is the King of heaven attended? He that containeth the world is laid in a stable;
responsory.repeat: Lying in a manger, reigning in heaven.

responsory.text: Unto us is born, this day, in the city of David, a Saviour, Which is Christ the Lord.
Lying in a manger, reigning in heaven.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
Lying in a manger, reigning in heaven.

latin.heading: Prídie Nonas Januárii Luna vicésima sexta. Anno Dómini 2027
entries: In Creta natális sancti Titi, qui, ab Apóstolo Paulo Epíscopus Creténsium ordinátus, et, post prædicatiónis offícium fidelíssime consummátum, finem beátum adéptus, in ea sepúltus est Ecclésia, ubi a beáto Apóstolo dignus miníster fúerat constitútus. Ipsíus tamen festívitas octávo Idus Februárii celebrátur.
Romæ sanctórum Mártyrum Prisci Presbýteri, et Priscilliáni Clérici, ac Benedíctæ, religiósæ féminæ; qui, témpore impiíssimi Juliáni, gládio martýrium complevérunt.

Item Romæ beátæ Dafrósæ, uxóris sancti Flaviáni Mártyris, ac matris sanctárum Bibiánæ et Demétriæ, Vírginum et Mártyrum; quæ, post interfectiónem viri sui, primum exsílio relegáta, deínde, sub præfáto Príncipe, cápite plexa est.
Bonóniæ sanctórum Hermétis, Aggæi et Caji Mártyrum, qui sub Maximiáno Imperatóre passi sunt.
Adruméti, in Africa, commemorátio sancti Mávili Mártyris, qui in persecutióne Sevéri Imperatóris, a sævíssimo Prǽside Scápula damnátus ad béstias, martýrii corónam accépit.
Item in Africa præclarissimórum Mártyrum Aquilíni, Gémini, Eugénii, Marciáni, Quincti, Theodóti et Tryphónis.
Apud Língonas, in Gállia, sancti Gregórii Epíscopi, miráculis clari.
Rhemis, in Gállia, sancti Rigobérti, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
latin.closing: Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.

translation.heading: January 4th 2027, the 26th day of the Moon
entries: The morrow is Octave of the Holy Innocents.
Upon the same 4th day of January, were born into the better life:

In Crete, holy Titus, whom the Apostle Paul ordained Bishop for the Cretans. When he had faithfully brought to an end (about the year 105), his work of preaching, he obtained a blessed death, and was buried in that church whereof the blessed Apostle had appointed him a worthy minister. His feast is kept upon the 6th day of the month of February.
At Rome, the holy martyrs the priest Priscus, the clerk Priscillian, and the devout woman Benedicta, who won martyrdom by the sword in the time of the wicked Emperor Julian (the Apostate).

Likewise at Rome, the blessed martyr Dafrosa, wife of the holy martyr Flavian (mother of St Bibiana). After the execution of her husband she was first sentenced to exile, and then put to death under the aforesaid Emperor Julian.
At Bologna, the holy martyrs Hermes, Aggaeus, and Caius, who suffered under the Emperor Maximian.

At Adrumetum, in Africa, the holy martyr Mavillus, whom the cruel President Scapula condemned to the wild beasts in the persecution under the Emperor Severus, and who thus received the crown of martyrdom.
Likewise in Africa, the illustrious martyrs Aquilinus, Geminus, Eugenius, Marcian, Quintus, Theodotus, and Tryphon (about end of fifth century).
At Langres, holy Gregory, bishop of that see, famous for miracles (in the year 539).
At Reims, in Gaul (in the year 743), the holy confessor Rigobert, bishop (in the year 722) of that see.
translation.closing: And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.

email.subject: Matins for Sunday 3 January: Dominica Secunda Nativitatis
email.preheader: What shall we say, then? shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?
email.html:
What shall we say, then? shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?

Matins · Sunday, 3 January 2027

Dominica Secunda Nativitatis

Dominica Secunda Nativitatis · Semiduplex

Read in Latin and English{{listen}}

Lesson I

Lesson from the letter of St. Paul the Apostle to the Romans

Rom 6:1-5

What shall we say, then? shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound? God forbid. For we that are dead to sin, how shall we live any longer therein? Know you not that all we, who are baptized in Christ Jesus, are baptized in his death? For we are buried together with him by baptism into death; that as Christ is risen from the dead by the glory of the Father, so we also may walk in newness of life. For if we have been planted together in the likeness of his death, we shall be also in the likeness of his resurrection.

℟. Behold the Lamb of God, behold Him Which taketh away the sins of the world; behold Him of Whom I said unto you: He That cometh after me is preferred before me * Whose shoe's latchet I am not worthy to unloose.

℣. He that is of the earth speaketh of the earth; He That cometh from heaven is above all.

℟. Whose shoe's latchet I am not worthy to unloose.

Lesson II

Rom 6:6-11

Knowing this, that our old man is crucified with him, that the body of sin may be destroyed, to the end that we may serve sin no longer. For he that is dead is justified from sin. Now if we be dead with Christ, we believe that we shall live also together with Christ: Knowing that Christ rising again from the dead, dieth now no more, death shall no more have dominion over him. For in that he died to sin, he died once; but in that he liveth, he liveth unto God: So do you also reckon, that you are dead to sin, but alive unto God, in Christ Jesus our Lord.

℟. This day which is breaking is holy; O come, ye Gentiles, and worship the Lord. * For this day is much light come down unto us from heaven.

℣. This is the day which the Lord hath made, let us rejoice and be glad in it.

℟. For this day is much light come down unto us from heaven.

Lesson III

Rom 6:12-18

Let no sin therefore reign in your mortal body, so as to obey the lusts thereof. Neither yield ye your members as instruments of iniquity unto sin; but present yourselves to God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of justice unto God.

℟. Blessed be He That cometh in the name of the Lord! God is the Lord Who hath showed us light. * Alleluia, Alleluia.

℣. This is the day which the Lord hath made, let us rejoice and be glad in it.

℟. Alleluia, Alleluia.

Lesson IV

For sin shall not have dominion over you; for you are not under the law, but under grace. What then? Shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace? God forbid. Know you not, that to whom you yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants you are whom you obey, whether it be of sin unto death, or of obedience unto justice. But thanks be to God, that you were the servants of sin, but have obeyed from the heart, unto that form of doctrine, into which you have been delivered. Being then freed from sin, we have been made servants of justice.

℟. This is he who comes, whose name no man knows but he himself; he is called the word of the Lord, dressed in shining clothes * And all the choirs of angels followed him, dressed in white.

℣. His eyes were as a flame of fire, and on his head were many diadems.

℟. And all the choirs of angels followed him, dressed in white.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. And all the choirs of angels followed him, dressed in white.

Lesson V

A sermon of St. Augustine, Bishop.

Serm. 13. de Tempore.

Our Lord Jesus Christ, dearest brethren, who in eternity is the Creator of all things, was as at this time born of a mother and became our Saviour. It was as at this time that he willed to be born for us in earthly time, so as to lead us to the Father's eternity.

℟. Rejoice with me, all ye that love the Lord. * For while I was yet little I pleased the Most High, and from my womb have I brought forth God and man.

℣. All generations shall call me blessed, for God hath regarded the lowliness of His hand-maiden.

℟. For while I was yet little I pleased the Most High, and from my womb have I brought forth God and man.

Lesson VI

℟. The heart of the Virgin was fixed, when the Angel declared unto her the mystery of God, and she conceived, then did she receive in her pure womb Him That is fairer than the children of men. * And, she that is blessed for ever, brought forth for us God and man.

℣. Soon rises, in that modest shrine, The Temple of the Lord Divine The stainless and unwedded one, Within her womb conceived the Son.

℟. And, she that is blessed for ever, brought forth for us God and man.

Man sinned and became guilty. God is born man, that the guilty may be delivered. Man fell, but God descended. Man fell miserably, God descended mercifully. Man fell by pride, God descended with grace.

℟. Blessed and worshipful art thou, O Virgin Mary; from thee, still maiden undefiled, the Saviour came a little Child. * He Whose glory filled the heavens lay in a manger.

℣. O Lord, I have heard thy speech and was afraid; I considered thy works and trembled. O Thou That dwellest between the two living creatures!

℟. He Whose glory filled the heavens lay in a manger.

℟. He came unto his own, and his own received him not. But as many as received him, he gave them power to be made the sons of God: * Who are born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.

℣. And if sons, heirs also; heirs indeed of God, and joint heirs with Christ.

℟. Who are born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. Who are born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.

From the Holy Gospel according to Matthew

In that time: When Herod was dead, behold an angel of the Lord appeared in sleep to Joseph in Egypt, Saying: Arise, and take the child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel. ℣. Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb.

℟. For thou hast borne in thy breast Him Whom the heavens cannot contain.

℟. The Virgin-Mother that knew not a man, bore, but travailed not. * She fed the Saviour of the world, The King of Angel hosts above, Jesus, our Redeemer blest, From the fountain of her breast.

℣. Soon rises in that modest shrine, The Temple of the Lord Divine; The stainless and unwedded one, Within her womb conceived the Son.

℟. She fed the Saviour of the world, The King of Angel hosts above, Jesus, our Redeemer blest, From the fountain of her breast.

He shall be called a Nazarene. The Evangelist, in quoting these words, saith that they were spoken by the Prophets, (Plural). If he had been citing any one precise passage he would have said by the Prophet, in the Singular. But he is citing the sense of the Prophets, and not any individual passage in any of their writings. He seemeth to refer to the fact that in Hebrew the word Nazarene signifieth holy, and that Christ is the Holy One of God is the common declaration of all the Scriptures.

℟. A child is born to us, and a son is given to us, and the government is upon his shoulder: * And his name shall be called, Wonderful, God the Mighty.

℣. His empire shall be multiplied, and there shall be no end of peace.

℟. And his name shall be called, Wonderful, God the Mighty.

Lesson XII

He seemeth to refer to the fact that in Hebrew the word Nazarene signifieth holy, and that Christ is the Holy One of God is the common declaration of all the Scriptures.

We can even state in a different way that which is written in the same words, according to the Hebrew text, in Iasiah: “There shall come forth a rod out of the root of Jesse, and the Nazarene shall rise up out of his root.”

℟. How is the King of heaven attended? He that containeth the world is laid in a stable; * Lying in a manger, reigning in heaven.

℣. Unto us is born, this day, in the city of David, a Saviour, Which is Christ the Lord.

℟. Lying in a manger, reigning in heaven.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. Lying in a manger, reigning in heaven.

Te Deum

Martyrology

Read at Prime today, announcing tomorrow

January 4th 2027, the 26th day of the Moon

The morrow is Octave of the Holy Innocents.

Upon the same 4th day of January, were born into the better life:

In Crete, holy Titus, whom the Apostle Paul ordained Bishop for the Cretans. When he had faithfully brought to an end (about the year 105), his work of preaching, he obtained a blessed death, and was buried in that church whereof the blessed Apostle had appointed him a worthy minister. His feast is kept upon the 6th day of the month of February.

At Rome, the holy martyrs the priest Priscus, the clerk Priscillian, and the devout woman Benedicta, who won martyrdom by the sword in the time of the wicked Emperor Julian (the Apostate).

Likewise at Rome, the blessed martyr Dafrosa, wife of the holy martyr Flavian (mother of St Bibiana). After the execution of her husband she was first sentenced to exile, and then put to death under the aforesaid Emperor Julian.

At Bologna, the holy martyrs Hermes, Aggaeus, and Caius, who suffered under the Emperor Maximian.

At Adrumetum, in Africa, the holy martyr Mavillus, whom the cruel President Scapula condemned to the wild beasts in the persecution under the Emperor Severus, and who thus received the crown of martyrdom.

Likewise in Africa, the illustrious martyrs Aquilinus, Geminus, Eugenius, Marcian, Quintus, Theodotus, and Tryphon (about end of fifth century).

At Langres, holy Gregory, bishop of that see, famous for miracles (in the year 539).

At Reims, in Gaul (in the year 743), the holy confessor Rigobert, bishop (in the year 722) of that see.

℣. And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.

℟. Thanks be to God.

Lesson I

De Epístola ad Romános

Lesson from the letter of St. Paul the Apostle to the Romans

Rom 6:1-5

Rom 6:1-5

Quid ergo dicémus? permanébimus in peccáto ut grátia abúndet? Absit. Qui enim mórtui sumus peccáto, quómodo adhuc vivémus in illo? An ignorátis quia quicúmque baptizáti sumus in Christo Jesu, in morte ipsíus baptizáti sumus? Consepúlti enim sumus cum illo per baptísmum in mortem: ut quómodo Christus surréxit a mórtuis per glóriam Patris, ita et nos in novitáte vitæ ambulémus. Si enim complantáti facti sumus similitúdini mortis ejus: simul et resurrectiónis érimus.

What shall we say, then? shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound? God forbid. For we that are dead to sin, how shall we live any longer therein? Know you not that all we, who are baptized in Christ Jesus, are baptized in his death? For we are buried together with him by baptism into death; that as Christ is risen from the dead by the glory of the Father, so we also may walk in newness of life. For if we have been planted together in the likeness of his death, we shall be also in the likeness of his resurrection.

℟. Ecce Agnus Dei, ecce qui tollit peccáta mundi: ecce de quo dicébam vobis: Qui post me venit, ante me factus est: * Cujus non sum dignus corrígiam calceaménti sólvere.

℟. Behold the Lamb of God, behold Him Which taketh away the sins of the world; behold Him of Whom I said unto you: He That cometh after me is preferred before me * Whose shoe's latchet I am not worthy to unloose.

℣. Qui de terra est, de terra lóquitur: qui de cælo venit, super omnes est.

Lesson II

Rom 6:6-11

Rom 6:6-11

Si autem mórtui sumus cum Christo, crédimus quia simul étiam vivémus cum Christo, Sciéntes quod Christus resúrgens ex mórtuis jam non móritur: mors illi ultra non dominábitur. Quod enim mórtuus est peccáto, mórtuus est semel: quod autem vivit, vivit Deo. Ita et vos existimáte vos mórtuos quidem esse peccáto, vivéntes autem Deo, in Christo Jesu Dómino nostro.

℟. This day which is breaking is holy; O come, ye Gentiles, and worship the Lord. * For this day is much light come down unto us from heaven.
